description: Preserve a frozen dashboard while completing a sign-in detour in Peek.
preconditions: Launch the completed Dev build with an isolated peek-auth profile.
Run python3 devutils/peek_auth_site.py and open http://127.0.0.1:8765/.
In the page context menu, enable Sign in with Peek on this site.
steps: Type an unsent draft, focus it, scroll down, and record URL, document identity, tick count, and scroll position.
Trigger Expire & sign in. Observe the still dashboard behind Peek, then sign in at the localhost identity provider.
After Peek reaches the deliberately wrong dashboard, close Peek with Escape. Check authenticated request on the original page.
Repeat with Test sessionStorage PKCE. Verify the callback can read the verifier, while source sessionStorage stays independent.
Cancel before signing in; verify no automatic repeated Peek. Retry with an explicit gesture.
Trigger Test memory-only state; use Continue in tab, then Fresh sign-in. Verify the live login page is retained and the original tab remains available.
While signed out, navigate to a new protected deep URL with query and hash. Sign in through Peek and close it. Verify the exact requested page loads once.
Repeat the uncommitted deep URL case but cancel login. Verify one recovery navigation and no repeated Peek.
Use Ordinary redirect. Disable the site toggle and repeat login; verify normal tab navigation.
Re-enable the toggle, quit normally, and relaunch. Verify the toggle persists and no temporary login Peek is restored.
Repeat in another profile and a private window. Verify auth storage is isolated from the regular profile.
Close a source tab with an unsent beforeunload draft while Peek is open, cancel the close, then close Peek and the browser normally.
observables: The existing source retains its WebContents and document identity, URL query and hash, draft, scroll, and focus.
The source receives freeze and resume lifecycle events and its timer does not advance between them.
Login uses the exact source profile. Authenticated requests work when the source resumes; the source is not unconditionally reloaded.
The copied sessionStorage verifier is available in Peek; callback writes do not overwrite source sessionStorage.
Source navigation and both automatic and external discard are blocked while auth Peek owns it.
Repeated auth redirects stay in one Peek; ordinary redirects do not open Peek.
Cancellation, promotion, tab switching, source close, and browser close release guards without crashes or lost beforeunload decisions.
A protected destination that never committed is retried once with query and hash intact.
Memory-only auth state cannot transfer to another page. Continue in tab preserves the live login page for a fresh sign-in.
